name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
principle: The product writes secrets, personal data, system details, or internal queries into a log file. Logs are often retained, aggregated, or less protected than primary data stores, creating an alternate path to sensitive data.
detection_signals: Java logger.info/debug/error/warn(...) concatenates password, token, secret, credential, ccn, ssn, accountNumber, location, cookie, Authorization, user object, or full query
Java Logger.getLogger(...).log(Level.*, message, ex) where message includes SQL query string, request body, credentials, or PII
Android Log.d/e/i/w(tag, ...) includes User.toString(), Location, Intent extras, account data, or exception text with sensitive values
C/C++ syslog(), fprintf(logFile,...), printf-style logging, spdlog, glog, or log4cxx call formats sensitive variable names such as password/token/key/card/ssn
Exception catch block logs raw exception plus sensitive context: log(... + request/response/user/query/body) or e.printStackTrace() to persistent log
Logging of HTTP headers or bodies containing Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-API-Key, access_token, refresh_token, or session id
Debug or verbose logging enabled in production config: DEBUG/TRACE level logs include secrets or PII
negative_signals: Logger call uses redaction helper such as mask(), redact(), sanitizeForLog(), or SensitiveDataMasker before the value reaches the log sink
Logged value is a constant event code/status string and does not concatenate or format sensitive variables
Credential or token is replaced with fixed placeholder such as "[REDACTED]" before logging
Allowlisted structured logging only records non-sensitive fields such as requestId, statusCode, operation, and duration
Production configuration disables DEBUG/TRACE and removes debug log files from deployment
Log files are access-controlled, but only as defense-in-depth and not relied on to permit secret logging
false_defense_traps: Relying on DEBUG level because production configuration can be changed or verbose logs can be shipped accidentally
Logging full objects via toString()/operator<< because future fields may add secrets or PII
Hashing secrets without salt or using reversible/base64 encoding before logging
Protecting log file permissions while still writing secrets into centralized logs, backups, or crash reports
Logging SQL queries with parameters because account numbers, usernames, schema, and query logic can still be exposed
verification_focus: Does any logging sink receive a raw sensitive value, full object, request/response body, exception context, or internal query without explicit redaction?

consequence_chains.trigger: Attacker or low-privileged user can read application, build, crash, or centralized logs
consequence_chains.consequence: Sensitive data is exposed to an unauthorized actor

consequence_chains.trigger: Logs expose SQL query text, table names, column names, or unparameterized query structure
consequence_chains.consequence: Database attack planning and SQL injection exploitation are simplified

patch_principle: Do not write secrets, credentials, PII, precise location, or full internal queries to logs.
Redact, mask, tokenize, or omit sensitive fields before any logging call.
Use allowlisted structured logging fields instead of logging full objects, requests, responses, or exceptions with context.
Disable debug/verbose logging and remove debug log files before production deployment.
Restrict log read/write permissions and retention as defense-in-depth.
